drills.q: What is Quarkus's build-time CDI-Lite DI container called?
What annotation routes a Quarkus REST method to a worker thread instead of the default Vert.x event loop?
Name the Mutiny type for a reactive stream of zero-to-many items, and its Reactor equivalent.
A native-image build fails at build time with a reflection-related ClassNotFoundException-style error. What's the mechanism, and what are the two fix options in order of preference?
drills.a: GraalVM's closed-world static reachability analysis couldn't prove a dynamically-loaded class/method reachable from the app's entry points, so it wasn't included in the compiled binary. Fix: prefer a Quarkus extension that already ships native-image metadata for that library; failing that, add explicit reflect-config.json entries.

drills.q: A team's Quarkus service passes all tests in `quarkus:dev` but throws a reflection error only when deployed as a native image on a rarely-hit code path. Explain why dev mode didn't catch it.
drills.a: quarkus:dev runs on the full JVM, where any reflective call works normally. Native image applies closed-world static reachability analysis at build time, which can fail to prove a reflective call site reachable -- a failure mode that literally does not exist in JVM/dev mode, so testing only there gives false confidence for native deployment.

drills.q: Why might a long-running, high-steady-throughput Quarkus service perform worse in native mode than in JVM mode, despite native's dramatically faster startup?
drills.a: Native image is AOT-compiled with every optimization decision fixed at build time -- no adaptation to actual live traffic. The JVM's JIT (C2) profiles real production traffic and progressively specializes hot paths over the process's lifetime, which can out-optimize AOT's build-time-only guesses at true steady state. Native's win is startup latency and idle memory, not necessarily peak sustained throughput.

drills.q: Design the framework choice for two new services: (a) an AWS Lambda function, (b) a long-running Kubernetes Deployment with steady, predictable traffic and no scale-to-zero requirement. Justify each.
drills.a: (a) Quarkus compiled to native image -- cold-start latency is directly billed and user-visible, and native's tens-of-milliseconds startup is decisive over a JVM cold start in the low seconds. (b) Spring Boot on the JVM is more defensible -- the process runs for hours/days between restarts so startup time amortizes to irrelevance, the JIT has time to pay off at steady state, and Spring's ecosystem depth reduces integration risk.

drills.q: A dependency has no documented GraalVM native-image support. List the options in order of preference before concluding the service can't go native.
drills.a: 1) Check for a Quarkus extension wrapping the library with native-image metadata already included. 2) Check the community graalvm-reachability-metadata project for an entry. 3) Hand-write reflect-config.json/resource-config entries by iteratively testing the native build. 4) Run that specific service in JVM mode instead -- native image is one feature of Quarkus, not mandatory for using the framework.

drills.q: What's the real design cost of choosing Panache's active-record style (PanacheEntity) over its repository style (PanacheRepository<T>)?
drills.a: Active-record couples the domain entity directly to persistence concerns (methods live on the @Entity class itself), making it harder to test business logic in true isolation from Hibernate and blurring separation of concerns -- more concise, but a real tradeoff, not a free win, versus the repository style's cleaner separation (closer to Spring Data's convention).

drills.q: Beyond faster startup, what's the deeper argument for ArC's build-time DI resolution over Spring's runtime resolution?
drills.a: Build-time resolution surfaces wiring errors (missing bean, ambiguous injection point) at build time / in CI rather than only at application startup in a deployed environment, or worse, only when a specific code path is first exercised in production -- shifting a class of bugs earlier in the pipeline. Spring's ApplicationContext also fails fast, but at runtime startup of that specific deployment, not at build time.

drills.q: A Quarkus bean's configuration value needs to come from a runtime environment variable unknown at build time. Does ArC's build-time DI model prevent this? Explain what's actually fixed at build time versus what can still vary at runtime.
drills.a: No, it doesn't prevent it. ArC fixes the EXISTENCE and wiring shape of beans at build time (which implementations get injected where), but individual configuration VALUES flowing into that fixed structure still resolve at runtime via Quarkus's config system (@ConfigProperty, MicroProfile Config) -- reading environment variables, config maps, or secrets normally. What ArC can't easily do is make a bean's very EXISTENCE conditional on a runtime-only value, unlike Spring's @ConditionalOnProperty, since the graph shape must be known before the runtime environment is.
